entries.title: PostgreSQL replication slot
entries.explanation: The slot records WAL retention and, for a logical slot, confirmed consumer progress. The position distance is not disk headroom or time to slot loss. Inactivity alone does not prove an abandoned consumer; these views do not measure subscription-worker processing.

fields.label: WAL bytes until risk of slot loss

entries.investigation: Identify the actual consumer and inspect restart and confirmed positions, WAL status and invalidation reason. Check synchronized-slot state and current server role separately. Confirm whether the consumer still needs the slot before changing retention.
entries.verify: Verify current WAL status and consumer confirmation, and check failover-slot synchronization separately. Account for slot recreation. A missing observation or field does not establish recovery or slot removal.

entries.title: Availability-group database replica
entries.explanation: These native database states are separate from replica and group health across other databases. They do not identify an application statement causing delay. Data movement is suspended. SQL Server can report zero secondary lag in this state; zero does not establish that the replica has caught up. The replica reports a disconnected replication connection. This does not identify a network fault or the database statement responsible. The last connection error is historical metadata; it does not by itself establish a current connection failure.

fields.label: Log send rate (KB/s, last active period)
Redo rate (KB/s of active redo time)

groups.title: Exact native log positions (not byte distances)
Availability group context across its databases

fields.label: Last connection error time (UTC offset unknown)

entries.investigation: Inspect the native database movement state and, only while suspended, its recorded reason. Compare independently observed replica connectivity and group health before testing a repair.
entries.verify: Compare new observations of the same group, database and replica after a tested repair. Preserve source visibility and native member context; a single point does not prove continuous recovery.

entries.title: Geo-replication link
entries.explanation: Lag and the last replication acknowledgment are primary-clock observations. The local commit time is a separate native fact, not an application-query owner.
entries.investigation: Check the exact link and local endpoint role, then compare the applicable native states and source visibility. Investigate native errors separately rather than attributing lag to a query.
entries.verify: Compare later native observations of this same link from the same endpoint role. Do not compare primary and secondary clocks as if they were one measurement.
